construction_notes.text: From the state Housing Element Annual Progress Report, through 2025.

State report rows for file MP22-003 (2022) give 333 W Virginia St and APN 264-35-039; the 2023 entitlement row gives 2315 Canoas Garden Ave and APN 456-25-005. Rows at 333 W Virginia St under SF22-033 and two ADU permits cover one single-family home and two ADUs, not this project.

City of San Jose permit MP22-003 (Ministerial Permit, folder year 2022), status Approved, issue date 2023-01-10: "SB 35 Ministerial Permit to allow the construction of two six-story buildings with up to 237 residential units (100% affordable, with a minimum of 60 units reserved for supportive housing), including State Density Bonus waivers for the elimination of step" (city text cut off at 255 characters)

City of San Jose permit MPA22-003-01 (Ministerial Permit, folder year 2025), status Under Review: "SB 35 Streamlined Ministerial Permit Amendment to decrease the number of units from 237 multi-family units to 80 multifamily units, including the reduction of the number of buildings from two to one; and associated landscaping changes for the project on a" (city text cut off at 255 characters)
City of San Jose permit T26-007 (Vesting Tentative Map, folder year 2026), status Under Review: "Tentative Map to subdivide one lot into two lots of future development of 79 workforce housing units."

San José Spotlight (2022-12-23): 237 apartments in two buildings on the Cathedral of Faith parking lot; Sand Hill estimated about $800,000 per apartment to build and planned to apply for city and state subsidies; SHP Christian Foundation committed undisclosed funds.

San José Spotlight (2025-01-23): the church plans 240 affordable homes in two complexes on its 13.4-acre property with Sand Hill Property Company and had raised about $13 million of roughly $200 million needed.
